title_en: Measures of the Chinese People's Liberation Army for Electing Deputies to the National People's Congress and Local People's Congresses at and above the County Level

articles.content_en: These Measures are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Constitution of the People's Republic of China and the Electoral Law of the National People's Congress and Local People's Congresses of the People's Republic of China.

Servicemen and women of the People's Liberation Army and other personnel participating in military elections shall, in accordance with these Measures, elect deputies to the National People's Congress and to the local people's congresses at or above the county level.

The People's Liberation Army and units at or above the regiment level of the People's Liberation Army shall establish election committees.
The Election Committee of the People's Liberation Army shall lead the election work of the entire army, and election committees at other levels shall preside over the election work of their respective units.
The servicemen committees of companies and other grassroots units shall preside over the election work of their respective units.

Servicemen and women of the People's Liberation Army, civilian staff, retired and demobilized personnel managed by the military, and other personnel shall participate in military elections.
If the garrison is located far from the residential areas of local residents and it is difficult for family members accompanying the military to participate in local elections, they may, with the approval of the election committee or the servicemen committee, participate in military elections.

Military representatives stationed in local factories, railways, water transport, scientific research units, and military personnel studying in local colleges and universities may participate in local elections.

Any person listed in Article 5 of these Measures who has reached the age of 18 shall have the qualifications of a voter and enjoy the right to vote and stand for election, regardless of ethnicity, race, gender, occupation, family background, religious belief, education level, property status, or length of residence.
Persons who have been deprived of political rights according to law shall not have the right to vote or stand for election.
A person with mental illness who is unable to exercise the right to vote shall, upon confirmation by the election committee, not participate in the election.

The members of the Election Committee of the People's Liberation Army shall be approved by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The members of election committees at other levels shall be approved by the election committee at the next higher level.
A lower-level election committee shall be under the leadership of the higher-level election committee.
The term of office of an election committee shall be five years, and it shall exercise its powers until a new election committee is formed. If a member of an election committee is transferred away from the unit or removed from office or retired, the position he or she holds in the election committee shall terminate automatically; if a member is no longer suitable to continue serving on the election committee due to adjustment of duties or other reasons, he or she shall be removed from the position on the election committee. When a vacancy occurs among the members of an election committee, a replacement shall be promptly made.

The Election Committee of the People's Liberation Army shall be composed of 11 to 19 members, with one chairperson, one to three vice-chairpersons, and a number of committee members. Election committees at other levels shall be composed of 7 to 17 members, with one chairperson, one to two vice-chairpersons, and a number of committee members.

An office shall be established under the election committee to specifically handle the daily work related to the election at the corresponding level.
The office shall be located in the political work department, and its staff shall be determined by the election committee at the same level.
The number of deputies to the National People's Congress to be elected by the People's Liberation Army shall be decided by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

The number of deputies to the National People's Congress to be elected by the departments of the Central Military Commission, theater commands, services and arms, the Academy of Military Sciences, the National Defense University, the National University of Defense Technology, and other units shall be allocated by the Election Committee of the People's Liberation Army. The organs directly under the Central Military Commission shall participate in the election of the department that manages them on its behalf.

The number of deputies to local people's congresses at or above the county level to be elected by the garrisons in various localities shall be decided by the standing committees of the people's congresses at the corresponding levels in the localities.
Matters concerning the election shall be decided through consultation between the provincial military commands (garrison commands, garrison areas), military sub-commands (garrison areas), and the people's armed forces departments, respectively, and the standing committees of the people's congresses in the localities.

For the election of deputies to the county people's congress by the garrisons, the servicemen and women stationed in that administrative area and other personnel participating in military elections shall directly elect them on the basis of electoral districts. The electoral districts shall be delineated according to the distribution of the garrison units within that administrative area.
The size of an electoral district shall be delineated on the basis of electing one to three deputies per electoral district.

Deputies to the people's congresses of cities divided into districts, autonomous prefectures, provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government to be elected by the garrisons shall be elected by servicemen congresses convened by units at or above the regiment level.
The servicemen congresses of the departments of the Central Military Commission, theater commands, services and arms, the Academy of Military Sciences, the National Defense University, and the National University of Defense Technology shall elect deputies to the National People's Congress.

Deputies to the servicemen congress of units at or above the division level of the People's Liberation Army shall be elected by the servicemen congress at the next lower level. If a lower-level unit does not convene a servicemen congress, the deputies shall be elected by the servicemen assembly.
Deputies to the servicemen congress of brigade and regiment level units shall be elected by servicemen assemblies convened by companies and other grassroots units.
The servicemen congress shall be convened by the election committee, and the servicemen assembly shall be convened by the election committee or the servicemen committee.
The term of office of each servicemen congress shall be five years. The term of office of deputies to the servicemen congress shall begin from the convening of the first meeting of the current servicemen congress and end at the convening of the first meeting of the next servicemen congress.

When the People's Liberation Army elects deputies to the National People's Congress and local people's congresses at or above the county level, candidates shall be nominated on the basis of electoral districts or electoral units.
Organizations of the Communist Party of China at various levels in the military may nominate candidates for deputies. Voters or deputies to the servicemen congress, jointly recommended by ten or more persons, may also nominate candidates for deputies. Recommenders shall introduce the candidates' information to the election committee or the servicemen committee. Recommended candidates for deputies shall truthfully provide their basic personal information to the election committee or the servicemen committee. If the basic information provided is untrue, the election committee or the servicemen committee shall notify the voters or deputies to the servicemen congress.

The election of deputies to the National People's Congress and local people's congresses at or above the county level by the People's Liberation Army shall adopt contested elections, and the number of candidates for deputies shall be greater than the number of deputies to be elected.
For direct election by voters, the number of candidates for deputies shall be one third to one time greater than the number of deputies to be elected; for election by the servicemen congress, the number of candidates for deputies shall be one fifth to one half greater than the number of deputies to be elected.

For direct election by voters, after the election committee or the servicemen committee has collected the candidates for deputies, it shall publish the list of candidates for deputies and their basic information 15 days before the election day, and submit them to the voters of the respective electoral districts for repeated discussion and consultation to determine the list of formal candidates for deputies. If the number of proposed candidates for deputies exceeds the maximum differential ratio specified in Article 19 of these Measures, the election committee or the servicemen committee shall submit them to the voters of the respective electoral districts for discussion and consultation, and determine the list of formal candidates for deputies based on the opinions of the majority of voters; if no relatively consistent opinion can be formed on the formal candidates, a preliminary election shall be conducted, and the list of formal candidates for deputies shall be determined according to the order of the number of votes obtained in the preliminary election. The list of formal candidates for deputies and their basic information shall be published seven days before the election day.
When a servicemen congress at or above the regiment level elects deputies to the people's congress, the time for nomination and deliberation of candidates for deputies shall not be less than two days. The election committee at that level shall print and distribute the list of candidates for deputies proposed according to law and their basic information to all deputies of the servicemen congress for deliberation and discussion. If the number of proposed candidates for deputies meets the differential ratio specified in Article 19 of these Measures, voting and election shall be conducted directly. If the number of proposed candidates for deputies exceeds the maximum differential ratio specified in Article 19 of these Measures, a preliminary election shall be conducted, and the list of formal candidates for deputies shall be determined according to the order of votes obtained in the preliminary election and the specific differential ratio determined by the servicemen congress at that level, followed by voting and election.

When a servicemen congress elects deputies to the National People's Congress and local people's congresses at or above the county level, candidates for deputies shall not be limited to deputies of the servicemen congress at that level.

The election committee or the servicemen committee shall introduce the information of candidates for deputies.
Organizations or individuals that recommend candidates for deputies may introduce the information of the recommended candidates at meetings of voter groups or groups of the servicemen congress.
In direct elections, the election committee or the servicemen committee shall, at the request of the voters, organize meetings between candidates and voters, where candidates shall introduce themselves and answer questions from voters. However, on the election day, any introduction of candidates for deputies must cease.

In direct elections, each electoral district shall convene a servicemen assembly to conduct the election, or set up polling stations in accordance with the principle of facilitating voters to vote. Voters who are scattered in location or have difficulty in mobility may vote in mobile ballot boxes. The voting and election shall be presided over by the servicemen committee or the election committee.
The voting and election of the servicemen congress shall be presided over by the election committee.

The election of deputies to the National People's Congress and local people's congresses at or above the county level by the People's Liberation Army shall uniformly adopt the method of secret ballot. During the election, a secret ballot writing area shall be set up.
If a voter is unable to fill in a ballot paper due to disability or other reasons, he or she may entrust a person he or she trusts to fill it in on his or her behalf.

If a voter is away during the election period, with the consent of the servicemen committee or the election committee, he or she may entrust another voter in writing to vote on his or her behalf. Each voter may accept no more than three such entrustments and shall vote in accordance with the entrusting voter's wishes.
A voter may cast a favorable vote, cast an opposing vote, vote for any other voter, or abstain from voting for candidates for deputies.

After the voting ends, the scrutineers and vote counters elected by the voters or by the deputies to the servicemen congress, together with personnel of the election committee or the servicemen committee, shall check the number of voters who voted and the number of votes, make a record, and have it signed by the scrutineers.
Close relatives of candidates for deputies shall not serve as scrutineers or vote counters.

If the number of votes cast in each election exceeds the number of voters who voted, the election shall be invalid; if it is equal to or less than the number of voters who voted, it shall be valid.
If the number of persons voted for on each ballot paper exceeds the prescribed number of deputies to be elected, the ballot paper shall be void; if it is equal to or less than the prescribed number, it shall be valid.

In direct elections, if the number of voters who participate in voting exceeds half of all voters in the electoral district, the election shall be valid. A candidate for deputy shall be elected only when he or she obtains more than half of the votes of the voters who participate in voting.
In elections by the servicemen congress, a candidate for deputy shall be elected only when he or she obtains more than half of the votes of all deputies.

If the number of candidates for deputies who have obtained more than half of the votes exceeds the number of deputies to be elected, those with the highest number of votes shall be elected. If two or more candidates have tied votes and it is impossible to determine the elected person, another vote shall be taken on the tied candidates, and the ones with the highest number of votes shall be elected.
If the number of elected deputies who have obtained more than half of the votes is less than the number of deputies to be elected, the remaining seats shall be filled in a separate election. In the separate election, a list of candidates shall be determined according to the order of the number of votes obtained in the first voting and in accordance with the differential ratio specified in Article 19 of these Measures. If only one person is to be elected, the candidates shall be two persons.
When separately electing deputies to a county people's congress in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the candidate for deputy with the highest number of votes shall be elected, provided that the number of votes obtained shall not be less than one third of the ballot papers; when separately electing deputies to people's congresses of cities divided into districts, autonomous prefectures, provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the National People's Congress by a servicemen congress at or above the regiment level, the candidate for deputy shall be elected only when he or she obtains more than half of the votes of all deputies of the servicemen congress.
The election committee or the servicemen committee shall determine whether the election result is valid in accordance with these Measures and shall announce it.

The deputies to the National People's Congress and local people's congresses at or above the county level elected by the People's Liberation Army shall be subject to the supervision of the voters and the original electoral units. Voters or electoral units shall have the right to recall the deputies they have elected.

For deputies to a county people's congress, if jointly requested by ten or more voters of the original electoral district, a written demand for recall may be submitted to the election committee at the brigade or regiment level.
The demand for recall shall state the reasons for the recall. The deputy proposed to be recalled shall have the right to present a defense at the servicemen assembly or submit a written defense.
The election committee at the brigade or regiment level shall print and distribute the demand for recall and the written defense of the deputy proposed to be recalled to the voters of the original electoral district.
The voting on the demand for recall shall be presided over by the election committee at the brigade or regiment level.

When a servicemen congress is in session, the election committee at or above the regiment level may submit a recall case against a deputy to the people's congress elected by the servicemen congress at that level. The recall case shall state the reasons for the recall.
When a servicemen congress is in session, the deputy proposed to be recalled shall have the right to present a defense at the meeting or submit a written defense. The recall case shall be deliberated at the meeting and then put to a vote.
The recall of a deputy shall be conducted by secret ballot.

The recall of a deputy to a county people's congress shall require approval by more than half of the voters of the original electoral district.
The recall of a deputy to a people's congress elected by a servicemen congress shall require approval by more than half of the deputies of the servicemen congress at that level.
The resolution on the recall shall be submitted to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level and the election committee at the next higher level in the military for recordation.

Deputies to the people's congresses of cities divided into districts, autonomous prefectures, provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the National People's Congress elected by the People's Liberation Army may submit a written resignation to the election committee of the original electoral unit. Deputies to county people's congresses elected by the People's Liberation Army may submit a written resignation to the election committee or the servicemen committee of the original electoral district.
Acceptance of a resignation shall require approval by more than half of all members of the servicemen congress or the servicemen assembly, and shall be reported to the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level and the election committee at the next higher level in the military for recordation.
If it is impossible to convene a servicemen congress due to tasks or other reasons, the election committee at or above the regiment level may accept the resignation of deputies to the people's congresses of cities divided into districts, autonomous prefectures, provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the National People's Congress elected at that level. After the election committee accepts the resignation of a deputy to the people's congress, it shall promptly notify the deputies of the servicemen congress that elected the deputy, and shall report to the standing committee of the people's congress at the corresponding level and the election committee at the next higher level in the military for recordation.

If a deputy's position becomes vacant during his or her term of office for any reason, a by-election shall be held in the original electoral district or original electoral unit.
If a deputy to a local people's congress at or above the county level elected by the People's Liberation Army is transferred out of that administrative area during his or her term of office, the qualifications of the deputy shall terminate automatically, and the vacancy shall be filled by a separate by-election.
In a by-election, the number of candidates for deputies may be greater than or equal to the number of deputies to be elected.
If it is impossible to convene a servicemen congress due to tasks or other reasons, a by-election may be conducted by the election committee at the same level.
The election expenses of the People's Liberation Army shall be borne by military funds.
The election of deputies to the National People's Congress and local people's congresses at or above the county level by the People's Armed Police Force shall be governed by these Measures.
